newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian firm sees voice as way to secure Internet.
newsitem.headline: Belgian firm sees voice as way to secure Internet.

text.p: Belgium's Keyware Technologies NV said it launched a voice recognition product which can be used to make transactions over the Internet secure.
In a statement Keyware said the heart of the product would be speech recognition software being developed by Belgian Nasdaq-listed speech products company Lernout & Hauspie .
"Development of the speech verification engine is in its final phase and first deliveries are expected during the second quarter of 1997," Keyware said.
The company said its Keyware S1 Security Server was being demonstrated this week at the CeBit fair in Hannover, Germany, and the Biometric Customer Identification Conference in Las Vegas, U.S.
Keyware, founded in 1996 and with offices in Brussels and Woburn, Massachusetts, aims to be the leading provider of biometric authentication technologies for enhanced security.
Biometrics is the use of body characteristics, such as hand or finger prints, or the eye's retina, to identify a person.
